Data quality · browser automation

Weekly Equipment Utilization

A local reporting workflow that brings fleet workbooks and equipment readings together while preserving data-quality checks, exceptions, and approved overrides.

  • RoleWorkflow design & development
  • TechnologyPython · Playwright · Excel
  • ContextProfessional work at Graham

The problem

A weekly report draws status and hour-meter information from fleet workbooks and an external manufacturer portal. Source files vary in layout, and missing, stale, or conflicting readings need a deliberate resolution before a report can be final.

Approach

I developed a local workflow that reads weekly fleet workbooks, maintains an editable equipment master, collects readings, and generates a workbook with draft or final status. A companion collector can resume after interruption, select the exact unit, retry a stuck step, and retain diagnostics.

Key decisions

  • Normalize equipment identity and source layout before calculations begin.
  • Define report windows and status rules in the process rather than relying on manual memory.
  • Use checkpoints and retries when external pages are unreliable.
  • Keep critical exceptions visible; approved overrides require a reason and approver.

What it demonstrates

Automation that anticipates imperfect inputs and unreliable web sources while keeping reviewability intact.
